text:
Session Overview - Presenting Issues
Alex reported persistent feelings of stress and frustration related to his recent relocation to Chicago and
the challenges of adjusting to a new environment. He shared that he often feels isolated and struggles to
form new connections, leading to a sense of loneliness.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Adjustment to Relocation
           ○ Alex discussed the difficulties of adapting to his new surroundings, including adjusting to a
               different work culture and social dynamics. He expressed frustration with feeling "out of
               place” and uncertain about his decision to move.
           ○ Explored strategies for developing a sense of stability and comfort in his new
               environment.
   2. Social Anxiety and Isolation
           ○ Alex described feelings of social anxiety, particularly in group settings, which has
               hindered his ability to make new friends. He mentioned that he avoids social events due
               to fear of rejection or judgment, and discussed past experiences with social anxiety and
               identified how it might be affecting his adjustment.

Therapist Observations

    ● Dr. Smith noted that Alex appeared withdrawn and showed signs of low energy when discussing
       his difficulties in adapting to his new environment.
    ● Alex often used self-deprecating language, indicating a lack of confidence in his ability to adjust
       successfully.

Therapeutic Interventions Used

    ● Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) - Cognitive Restructuring: Helped Alex identify and
challenge negative self-perceptions about his social interactions.
    ● Social Skills Training: Practiced techniques for initiating conversations and building rapport
        with new acquaintances.
    ● Mindfulness Practices: Introduced exercises to help Alex stay present and reduce feelings of
        overwhelm in social situations.
    ● Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT): Worked on setting small, attainable goals for Alex to
        gradually increase his comfort in social settings.

Goals and Action Plan

    ● Short-term goals: Attend at least one social event or activity in the coming week to practice the

skills discussed in therapy.
   ● Long-term goals: Build a supportive social network in his new environment and enhance his
      confidence in social interactions.

Homework/Reflection

   ● Reflect on moments when he feels socially anxious, noting any specific thoughts and
      re-evaluating them with more balanced perspectives.
   ● Practice one mindfulness exercise daily to manage stress and reduce feelings of isolation.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Following his short-term goal plan, Alex reported going out to a bar on a Monday night to reduce his
social anxiety. There he met a nurse named Lucia, and they chatted and played darts. Despite exchanging
numbers, Alex felt too anxious to reach out to her.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Adjusting to Unfamiliar Environments
          ○ Alex has previously stated his inability to adjust to new environments. Forcing himself to
              go to a bar on Monday night allowed him to face his anxieties about feeling out of place.
              Alex reported having a good time despite some initial anxiety at the beginning of the
              night.
   2. Sabotaging Relationships
            ○ Although Alex had a good time with Lucia, he did not reach out to her. His fear of
              rejection has manifested in a way that prevents Alex from forming meaningful
              relationships. He believes he will be rejected eventually, so he purposefully didn’t reach
              out as a way to avoid a negative outcome.

Therapist Observations

    ● Dr.Smith observed that Alex has shown improving signs since last session by engaging in
       conversations with strangers and stepping out of his comfort zone by going to the bar on a
       Monday night
    ● Despite Alex’s improvement, his self-deprecating language has gotten worse indicating is lack of
       confidence needs improvement

Goals and Action Plan

    ● Short-term: Take initiative to follow up on social plans once this week, like going out for drinks
       with coworkers.
    ● Long-term: Get comfortable with rejection in order to create long lasting relationships.

Homework/Reflection:

    ● Reflect on moments where he feels like avoiding social situations.
    ● Practice one mindfulness exercise daily to manage stress and reduce feelings of isolation.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex’s therapy sessions have begun to consist of working around his social anxiety and becoming more
carefree. He has just moved to the Northside of Chicago, and he wants to explore and meet more people.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Exploring new places
           ○ Alex had worked on adjusting to new environments. He’s expressed a desire to explore
              his new neighborhood as well as places nationally. Instead of simply adjusting to new
              environments, it will be productive for him to actively seek out unfamiliar environments
              to minimize his anxiety.

Therapist Observations

    ● Alex has made strides coping with his anxiety. He has expressed his desire to explore and meet
       new people.
    ● Alex expresses the desire to be more carfree. Alex still speaks about Lucia, and how he would
       like to meet someone as easygoing and easy to talk to as her, as she’s just now a ‘distant
       memory’.

Goals and Action Plan
   ● Short term: Work on being more carefree.
   ● Long term: Alex will be more comfortable putting himself out there in new environments and
       with new people.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Plan and save for 3 vacations as milestones for putting himself out there.
   ● Prevent overthinking by using mindfulness techniques.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex described his 5-day trip to California from September 28th to October 2nd. He states that he enjoyed
it a lot, and put himself in a lot of situations where he was able to socialize with others and converse while
having a good time. He took a lot of pictures. Once Alex gets back from California, he begins to drive
back to his apartment from Midway Airport. He somehow ended up rear-ending Maya Caldwell on
Lakeshore. They exchange numbers for insurance, the police come and file a report, and both Maya and
Alex get checked out at St. Murky's. In the ER, a doctor examines Maya, and then Alex. After
examination, Maya notices that Alex is in the next bed over, and they begin talking. She takes a quick nap
after their conversation while waiting for the doctor. The doctor then examines Alex, relaying that he has
no injuries. He is discharged. Alex also thought Maya was cute and decided to shoot his shot. He writes a
note “Sorry ‘bout the accident, would love to make it up to ya ;)” with his phone number, and leaves the
hospital.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Taking initiative to make plans with someone
           ○ Due to his social anxiety, Alex has had issues making plans to meet with someone.
               Leaving a sticky note expressing interest to meet up with Maya was a great way to get
               over his fear of rejection.
   2. Experiencing unexpected situations
           ○ Alex has anxiety over new environments, but sometimes unexpected situations will
               happen that will force him out of his comfort zone. Alex did not mean to rear end
               Maya, but in doing so he had to face his social anxiety to resolve the situation. The trip
               Alex took helped with his anxiety which was part of the reason he handled the situation
               well.

Therapist Observations

    ● Dr.Smith observed Alex’s calm reaction to the car accident. Alex has made improvements with
       his goal to be more care free. He was able to handle a stressful situation without being
       overwhelmed.
    ● Alex has made improvements with his social anxiety. He has expressed an interest in engaging in
       conversations with strangers like he did with Lucia. When given the chance to put himself out
       there, he took it by leaving the sticky note.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Practice mindfulness exercises to cope with anxiety over the outcome of leaving the sticky note.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex’s session with Dr. Sam Smith consists of him talking about his ‘date’ with Maya. Alex states that:
Alex and Maya meet up for drinks, but Maya plays hard to get. After the date, Alex tells Maya he would
love to take her out again. Maya kindly declined, stating that she was only home to visit her family. Alex
described Maya as a social butterfly, always being able to talk to people confidently, but at the same time
always being willing to spread information, both good and bad.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Managing Disappointment
          ○ Alex’s date with Maya did not go as he had planned. Alex felt like Maya was flakey and
             insincere. Alex had hoped for a deeper connection, but he was left disappointed when
             Maya did not live up to his expectations. Perhaps he feels cheated in a way since he put
             himself out there and he was shut down.

Therapist Observations
   ● Dr. Sam Smith notes that Alex has not talked about Lucia and that this is progress from the last
      couple of weeks.
   ● He thought that Maya was out to play games and create some drama with him, seeing that she
      played with his feelings. The more Alex talked about Maya, the more he seemed both hurt and
      slightly angry that he did not appreciate the way she ‘manipulated’ him.
   ● Alex should find ways to manage his emotions and anxiety with situations like this.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Alex should reflect on situations where he feels wronged by someone. He should think of the
      other person’s perspective, and he should ask himself why he feels angry and/or hurt by their
      actions.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex’s session with Dr. Sam consists of him talking about his second trip. He considers this trip to be a
self-discovery trip, where he took a road trip all over State Route One and solo hiked.

Key Themes and Discussion Points
   1. Self-discovery
             ○ Traveling alone has allowed Alex a chance to take risks and do things that might make
              him anxious. By facing his anxieties head on, Alex has been able to practice his coping
                skills. As a result, his anxieties have diminished, and his confidence has improved.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex talks about his trip as very refreshing. It’s clear that stepping out of his comfort zone has
      allowed him to have more confidence in himself. Setting aside time for himself has also helped
      him to reflect on his emotions creating a stronger sense of self.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Make an effort to ground himself when he feels anxious. Alex should remind himself of his
       successful adventures and his coping skills when he feels anxious in everyday life.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex’s session with Dr. Sam consists of him talking about his third and final trip to New York. He talks
about it so highly, as he mentions Lucia once again. He states that: He was in a random bar with a group
of friends he met a couple of days into the trip, and he ran into Lucia. She stated that she was there for a
work trip, and they began to talk about their lives ever since they last saw each other. Alex believes that it
is his chance of making a move this time, and decides to ask her out. They wait till they both go back to
Chicago to go on their date. He noticed that she was not as stressed as the first time they met and that she
had changed career fields, which he thought was interesting. He remembers Lucia saying how she chose
her career because of how interested she was in babies and how much she cared about her patients.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Follow through with his plans with Lucia in order to manage his fear of rejection. ● Practice
   mindfulness exercises if Alex experiences disappointment with Lucia like he did with Maya.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex’s session with Dr. Sam Smith was a pretty good session. Alex talks about his first date with Lucia to
Navy Pier and shows him some pictures. He then states how he asked her out and that they began dating.
Alex states that Lucia is kind and cares for the people she works with. In regards to Alex’s social anxiety,
they did not really talk about that much as he just continued talking about Lucia.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex has shown improvement with his social anxiety by asking Lucia to be his girlfriend.
   ● Alex’s anxiety and worrying seems to have decreased. Instead of dwelling on bad scenarios, his
   focus is on the positives like his date with Lucia.

Homework/Reflection
   ● To maintain a healthy relationship with Lucia, practice good communication and be mindful of
      each other’s boundaries.
   ● When feeling anxious, practice breathing exercises. Right down any instances of relationship
      anxieties to talk about in the next session.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex talks to Dr. Sam Smith about his surprise birthday party for Lucia. He states that while he is at Party
City, he bumps into Maya. They catch up. Alex states how he is in a very happy relationship, and he can
see this being long-term. Maya is happy for him, however she overshadows and interrupts him by going
on and on about her life. She is also in a very happy relationship with this guy named Eric, and how it was
fate for them two to meet and be together. She talks to Alex (one-sided conversation), and then realizes
she is running late to a couple of plans. She wishes him farewell and leaves. Alex feels as if it was a bit
rude, but ultimately decides to brush it off, as he would probably never see her again. Alex also states how
he brought this moment up to Lucia, who ultimately responded quite well. She stated that what happened
in the past stays in the past, and was a quote that stuck with Alex. He admires that she is truly a person
who is present in the moment.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex has made progress by being able to identify and overcome an unprecedented yet subtle
      situation when he felt Maya was a bit rude to him.
   ● Alex seems to be managing his relationship anxiety well. He communicated with Lucia, and he
      was able to recognize and accept her mature response.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex talks to Dr. Sam Smith about how nervous he is about proposing to Lucia. Session after session,
Alex finds something good to talk about. He said that Lucia has been with him through the better and the
worse, and he would like to take the next big steps with her. Dr. Sam Smith gives some advice, and Alex
is on his way.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex’s anxiety has improved significantly since the first session. He is able to manage his anxious
      thoughts, and as result, his relationship with Lucia has been steady.
    ● Alex is able to step outside his comfort zone. He used to struggle with this, but by taking a huge
          step in his life by proposing, he has shown that he can manage change and uncertainty.

Homework/Reflection
   ● When anxious thoughts arise about the proposal and the future, notice the thoughts as just thoughts.
      Instead of trying to correct the thoughts or dwell on them, accept them for what they are – just
      thoughts not reality.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex is flabbergasted when he comes into his therapy session. Alex states how Lucia just told him that she
was pregnant with twins and that she had already gone to an OB appointment to confirm. He said he was
speechless, and felt that at the bottom of his heart, he was not really happy about this. He states that he
finally began to have some consistency in his life, and that kids were not in the picture for another year or
two. He also stated that even though this was taken with many surprises, he always prefers things in even
numbers, no matter if it is children, food, miles, etc. He thinks that singular objects are very much bad
luck.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex is experiencing anxiety over something unexpected again. His fear of change is manifesting
      again since he feels unhappy about the surprise pregnancy.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Be considerate of Lucia’s feelings. This situation is something shared between Lucia and Alex.
      Be honest with her, but be mindful of how words can come across to her while she’s in this
      vulnerable position.
   ● When feeling anxious and depressed, focus on what is in his control. Unexpected things are out of
      his control, but his reaction to it is within his control. Practice this mindful exercise to manage
      anxious thoughts.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex talks about his past OB appointments with Lucia and his recent position promotion. He talks about
vanishing twin syndrome, and how that happened to his wife. He is very sad, but in all honesty, he states
that it is sort of a relief not to have to work as hard as he projected to be to provide twins with a
satisfactory life. Alex continues to go on about how his job now requires more on-call hours, which is
something he is still new to. Seeing how he will be saving up for a kid though, he is willing to take the job
to have more pocket money. He is unable now to attend all the OB appointments but is able to take Lucia
there or pick her up usually if it aligns with him getting off of work. He is also back to a point where he
does not have much time to socialize and is physically seen to be more tired than he used to be.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex stated he doesn’t have to work as hard to provide for twins. It’s a bit odd to phrase caring for
      children that way.
   ● Alex is spending more time working which is impacting his mentally and physically.

Homework/Reflection

    ● Alex should incorporate rest time in his schedule. Relaxing on Friday evenings is a good place to
       start.
     ● Alex should also incorporate time to socialize with friends and Lucia. Working a lot can make
       him more depressed. Aim to set time aside to socialize with someone at least once a week.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex talks to Dr. Sam Smith about how he suggested that Lucia go to a therapist, as she has been very sad
lately, but she was not willing to. She went off on Alex and they have not been talking for the past couple
of days. Alex states that Lucia is beginning to expect more of his role as a husband and father to their
future baby. He states that he thinks Lucia is beginning to blame him for the loss of their second child,
and that he would do anything to fix this issue, even if it meant adopting another newborn.

Therapist Observations
   ● Alex is seen to be more exhausted and is only looking for solutions for his wife instead of him. ●
   Lucia’s grief has caused her to lash out at Alex. Alex’s past issues with relationship anxiety and
   rejection has made her extra sensitive to her anger.

Homework/Reflection
   ● Dr. Sam Smith suggests Alex take a day off. Alex is experiencing a lot of stress from work and
   from his family life. Taking time for himself should help him manage his stress and anxiety. ● Set
   boundaries with Lucia. She is grieving and needs support from her husband, but if she continues to
   lash out, Alex should try to calmly tell her he needs space.

Session Overview - Presenting Issues

Alex comes into the session with a smile, stating that his child was born yesterday, however their baby
was born prematurely. He has taken the day off of work to stay with Lucia for the pregnancy, however is
also complaining about the lack of paternity leave within his job atmosphere, expecting him to be working
a lot more than he expected. With not having the time to find another job, Alex describes his situation as
being stuck. Dr, Sam Smith suggests that they go over his lifestyle to find ways to combat burnout. They
do that for the remainder of the session.



Therapist Observations
   ● Alex is a combination of being tired, happy, and anxious at the same time.
     ● Alex hasn’t had a lot of time to process his emotions since he is busy with work and his family.

Homework/Reflection
   ● To combat burnout, Alex should try journaling. Writing down his thoughts and feelings will help
      him process them.
   ● Staying active will help Alex feel less mentally tired. Doing yoga and light exercise like going for a
       walk daily should help improve his mood.
